What was learned and saved:

The error was a Gini-coefficient convention mistake, not a data-extraction error. My answer (0.006) was exactly half the gold (0.012). For a 2-value set, the population Gini = |a−b|/(2(a+b)) while the sample/unbiased Gini (with the n/(n−1) correction) = |a−b|/(a+b) — exactly 2× larger. OfficeQA grades against the sample convention. The surplus/deficit half (receipts > expenditures ⇒ surplus) was correct.

Saved:
- New reference file `references/gini-coefficient-small-set.md` with the formulas, the worked failure, the recipe, and pitfalls.
- A pointer in the skill's SKILL.md reference list.
- A compact memory note (merged onto the delimiter entry since memory was full): use SAMPLE Gini (÷n(n−1)), 2 values = |a−b|/(a+b) = 2× population.

This is generalizable — any future Gini question on a small value set will otherwise hit the same exact-2× error.
